newsitem.title: UK: Lufthansa Cargo to tackle no-show problem.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Cargo to tackle no-show problem.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG (LCAG), the autonomous cargo arm of Deutsche Lufthansa AG, is in the process of establishing a Frankfurt-based space control project in an effort to reduce "no-show" shipments, said its UK and Ireland marketing manager Ruediger Helm.

He told Reuters that four stations -- London, Tokyo, Hong Kong and Chicago -- had been designated as "pilot stations" in order to find ways and means of cutting down on the number of shipments booked by freight forwarders but which fail to arrive.
"No-shows' are not a big problem for us in Britain, but they certainly are in Frankfurt, especially concerning shipments booked on (Boeing 747) freighter flights to Tokyo and Seoul," said Helm.
"The aim of this project is to establish a statistical base highlighting the problem areas and getting to grips with the whole 'no-show' question," he said.

He added that when particular routes suffering from persistent "no-shows" had been identified, local managers would be given leeway to allow for a certain amount of over-booking in order to fill space that would otherwise be unused.
Air Canada has just introduced penalty charges on forwarders for cargo "no-shows" in Europe but Helm said Lufthansa Cargo's initiative was unrelated to this development.
